name: CVS Health
description: CVS Health has three big engines that also trade with each other. Aetna (Health Care Benefits) is a health insurer: it collects premiums ($134.8B in 2025) from employers, individuals and government programs and pays medical claims, keeping the spread; 26.6 million medical members, of whom 4.3 million are in Medicare Advantage. CVS Caremark (Health Services) is a pharmacy benefit manager for about 87 million plan members: it processes about 1.9 billion prescription claims a year for employers and health plans, and also runs primary-care and clinic businesses (Oak Street Health, MinuteClinic). The Pharmacy & Consumer Wellness segment is about 9,000 CVS drugstores that dispensed about 28.5 percent of all US retail pharmacy prescriptions. Segments sell to each other, so $71.6B of segment revenue is eliminated to reach $402.1B consolidated revenue. Profit is thin (adjusted operating margin 3.6 percent, computed 14,443 / 402,067); Aetna's adjusted operating income was $307M in 2024 vs $5.6B in 2023, and $2.9B in 2025.

gics.note: SEC SIC code 5912 (Retail-Drug Stores and Proprietary Stores). CVS is an insurer (Aetna), a drug-benefit middleman (Caremark) and a drugstore chain in one company; the source's one sub-industry label also covers Quest and Labcorp. About 70.5 percent of pre-elimination segment revenue is insurance (Aetna) and PBM (computed).

businessLines.name: Health Services (Caremark PBM, clinics and care delivery)
businessLines.shareBasis: Share of revenue = 190,425 / 473,630 (sum of the four reported segments before the $71,563M intersegment elimination); the segments therefore do not sum to consolidated $402,067M. Share of profit = 7,151 / 16,130 (three operating segments' adjusted operating income, before Corporate/Other of -$1,687M).
businessLines.how: Employers, health plans and government programs pay Caremark to manage their drug benefit: it negotiates discounts from drug makers and retail pharmacy networks, applies formularies, and the reported revenue includes the drug cost and retail co-payments passed through, so revenue is huge and the margin small. Volume is prescription claims processed: 1,900.7M in 2025, down from 2,344.3M in 2023. The clinic and primary-care lines are paid by insurers and Medicare per patient or visit.
businessLines.description: PBM solutions through CVS Caremark (claims processing, formularies, mail and specialty pharmacy fulfilment services to plan clients) plus health care services in medical clinics, virtually and at home (Oak Street Health primary care for Medicare patients, MinuteClinic).

revenue.note: Before intersegment eliminations; FY2024 $173,605M; FY2023 $186,843M; H1 2026 $100,032M vs $89,915M. Includes about $10.9B of retail co-payments (FY2024 $11.4B, FY2023 $13.7B).

businessLines.shareBasis: Same basis as Health Services (share of the pre-elimination segment sum, and of the three operating segments' adjusted operating income).
businessLines.how: Employers, individuals and government programs pay a monthly premium per member and Aetna pays the medical claims; profit is what is left after claims and operating costs. The medical benefit ratio (share of premiums paid out as care) was 91.2% in 2025 vs 92.5% in 2024, 87.4% in Q2 2026 vs 89.9% in Q2 2025. Self-funded employers (administrative services contracts) pay a fee and bear the claims risk themselves.
businessLines.description: Aetna health insurance: commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, Medicaid, stand-alone Medicare Part D drug plans, and administrative services for self-funded employers.
